prompt:
Draw exactly ONE new Small Seal font glyph from the attached reference image. It shows FOUR historical specimen slots of the SAME character labelled THX, CCZ, QJZ and DYC; any slot marked UNAVAILABLE is absent evidence. Study ALL AVAILABLE specimens equally. Reconstruct one coherent attested whole form with the original ancient identity; do not combine incompatible variant components, imitate only THX, or substitute a modern Chinese character.

Build genuine smooth stroke trajectories as original harmonious Gothic monoline drawing, with absolutely CONSTANT stroke width around 3% of the full canvas. All strokes must share that width, with round caps and round joins, smooth rounded curves and precise straight bars, no taper, swelling, brush outlines, serifs, pressure modulation, textures or blobs. Keep every required counter and gap clearly open. Essential bar length relationships, branches, descending legs, tiny detached marks and contacts are structural requirements, not decoration.

Use a square 1:1 canvas. Center the ONE glyph inside the central70% with generous clear margins. Output ONLY pure BLACK constant-width strokes on a fully TRANSPARENT background, with no labels, text, codepoint, chart, grid, background, frame, shadows, watermark or multiple specimens. Exactly one complete glyph.

Explicit structural/proportion reading aid:
U+3D078. LEFT separate vertical stem carries three horizontal bars; bottom bar modestly longest, top about85–90% of bottom, middle shortest. RIGHT TOP: a detached peaked roof made of two smooth diagonals. A SHORT separate horizontal bar sits below the peak, about45% of full roof width; choose coherent THX/CCZ/DYC OPEN roof variant, so this short bar must NOT touch either roof side or create a closed triangular field. Below roof are FOUR major descending courses. At lower-left a short upright curves down-left and has exactly THREE short inward/right-facing arms. The first/upper and third/lower arms end FREELY. The MIDDLE arm alone reaches rightward to join the next course. That next course starts as a small hook curling left at upper end, bends right/down in an S-like shape and descends as a long curved stem to baseline. Keep the gap between the left upright top and S upper hook; joined only at middle arm, not enclosed counters. To the RIGHT of this S stem are exactly TWO independent long gently outward-curving downstrokes, with no branches or crossbars. The inner one descends longest; far-right one ends a little higher. Thus right lower inventory is branched left upright + S stem + two unbranched right descenders, FOUR lower courses total. Preserve all three left branch tips, middle contact, roof gap and detached roof interior bar.

Open roof and detached short interior bar; no closed roof triangle in chosen THX/CCZ/DYC variant.
Right lower four courses: branched left stem with three right arms, S stem, two independent unbranched descenders.
Only middle left arm contacts S; first/third arms remain free, no invented lower counters.
notes: All four references and enlarged forms compared. Native preserves open roof, four lower courses and three left branch terminals with just middle contact.
Two far-right descenders remain independent; inner one longest, outer ends higher.
caveats: QJZ closes its roof and some lower fields through source-specific contacts. Native retains coherent open THX/DYC-type contacts rather than mixing alternatives.
